State for 3.0.0_SA_CVO at L9: which shape you took and why, including what you rejected; whether a reader of the published artifact can distinguish an automatic publish from a hand one, measured on a REAL artifact rather than argued; what human dependency remains, if any, and what would remove it; and whether your mechanism has a blind spot analogous to the commit-trigger one named in this face. acceptance.output_evidence: Full text in the result document, section 'O28-AC2 -- JUDGMENT'. SUMMARY OF WHAT IS RECORDED THERE. (1) WHICH SHAPE AND WHY: shape (i), the recurring device-side timer, because the L4 ruling @46b832a9a3 withdrew the other two and left no other carrier. REJECTED BEYOND THE WITHDRAWN SHAPES: a logon trigger (it would have closed the coverage gap cheaply and made arm (d) read better while making the mechanism worse, and the order kills habit-dependent cadence by name); a SYSTEM/group principal (denied by measurement, and it would move the credential source out from under the scoped-role assume that bound (63) forbids widening); a hand publish to hold the report green (forbidden by bound (61), and it would have destroyed the evidence arm (a) rests on -- the artifact sat 18.3 h stale and I let it). (2) CAN A READER DISTINGUISH AUTOMATIC FROM HAND, MEASURED ON A REAL ARTIFACT? YES, and measured rather than argued: trigger_chain in the SERVED bytes terminates at wininit.exe through services.exe and svchost.exe, an ancestry a shell-launched run cannot have; the same detector in a human-started process reads interactive on the same code. (3) WHAT HUMAN DEPENDENCY REMAINS AND WHAT WOULD REMOVE IT: the interactive-only principal, removed by ONE elevated line stated verbatim with its one-line rollback; the device being off, which no device-side carrier can remove; and the S4U network-credential question, which only an OBSERVED FIRE under the new principal answers -- not the write's own output, since Set-ScheduledTask self-reports success on a non-terminating failure. (4) BLIND SPOT ANALOGOUS TO THE COMMIT TRIGGER? YES, AND A DIFFERENT SHAPE, NAMED PRECISELY RATHER THAN CLAIMED SYMMETRIC. The commit trigger's defect was ANTI-CORRELATION -- it sampled when drift was lowest. A quarter-hour timer samples on wall-clock time, which is INDEPENDENT of how much drift exists, so it is not anti-correlated. Its blind spot is CORRELATED-WITH-PRESENCE: it runs only while a session exists, and a session existing is POSITIVELY correlated with someone writing files, so the gap covers the hours when drift is least likely to be changing -- the benign direction of the same family. NOT OFFERED AS A CLEAN BILL: a long logged-out stretch is exactly when a device left mid-work sits with uncommitted material and reports nothing, and an absent reading and a clean tree still render the same way to the consumer -- the quiet-versus-silent confusion OS-s-21's accept was re-cut to prevent. The 26 h ceiling is what converts that silence into a visible verdict and it is untouched. HONEST STATEMENT: the mechanism narrows the window from 24 h to minutes while someone is logged on and does NOTHING when nobody is, and the second half is the elevated line rather than a property of the shape. (5) VOLUNTEERED LIMITATION OF MY OWN INSTRUMENT: _trigger_evidence() returns 'interactive' as a FALLBACK, not as positive evidence -- it is really 'no scheduler ancestor found'. The positive half of the discrimination (scheduled) is genuine; the negative half is a default, so a future launcher that is neither a shell nor the Task Scheduler would be labelled interactive on no evidence. 'unknown' covers only an UNREADABLE chain, not an UNRECOGNISED one.

mutant.description: FOUR controls, because three of this battery's claims could otherwise have been constants. (1) THE S4U DENIAL could have meant 'the task is locked' rather than 'this principal needs elevation' -- so the SAME session, SAME cmdlet, SAME call shape was run with an Interactive principal on a FRESH task as a positive control. (2) THE TRIGGER DISCLOSURE could be a self-report a hand caller can forge -- so a MUTANT was run: a hand process DECLARING '--trigger scheduled' while its real ancestry says otherwise. (3) THE AGREEMENT FIELD could encode non-evaluation as a verdict -- so the unreadable-chain case was exercised in BOTH declaration directions. (4) THE ARM-FAILURE PATTERN itself: three arms raised at once and three held, so the denominator of failing arms was compared against what they SHARED rather than debugged one at a time.

(4) The three failing arms must share a dependency the three holding arms do not touch.

determinism.method: Five of six arms are deterministic given a fixed world: (a) reads an immutable S3 VERSION LIST plus a committed XML, (c) (e) and (f) read committed bytes and the live task definition, and (d) reads the task's own gating fields. ARM (b) IS DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED, and that is a property of the subject rather than a defect: the served artifact is REPUBLISHED every quarter hour, so its VersionId and LastModified differ on every run. The arm therefore asserts on the SHAPE of the process ancestry -- a scheduler ancestor present, zero human-session ancestors -- and never on a fixed VersionId, which is what lets it stay true across the very cadence it exists to prove. An arm pinned to one VersionId would read a snapshot and would go stale 15 minutes later.
